boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Yellow Tavern record (May 11, 1864) in Grant's Overland Campaign [May-June 1864]. The Beaver Dam, Ashland and Meadow Bridge actions of May 9–12 are the same raid, not this record. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Divisions and the live field zero. NPS calls the Confederate cavalry outnumbered. Sheridan's 1866 report says he began the campaign with about 10,000 (the noun is garbled in OCR) and the same number of horses in passable trim, and later that the enemy's cavalry was superior in numbers during the period. Humphreys says Sheridan's three divisions moved on Yellow Tavern and that Fitzhugh Lee's division of two brigades was moving to interpose, while Gordon's brigade followed the rear.
claims.rationale: NPS's 'outnumbered' and Sheridan's period-wide claim conflict; Sheridan's 10,000 is a May 4 figure for the corps. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Sheridan says he gained the Brook turnpike, took two guns and drove the enemy about 4 miles; NPS and Sheridan's report say Stuart was mortally wounded. Humphreys says Stuart was mortally wounded and Brigadier General James B. Gordon killed.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Gordon's wounding at Meadow Bridge the next day is outside this record.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 800 total; the live field reads zero. Sheridan's May 13 dispatch expects wounded not over 250 and total losses not over 350 for the raid; his May 25 dispatch gives 379 wounded from May 9 to 25, with between 75 and 80 captured; his report and Humphreys give 425 casualties on the march. Humphreys found no Confederate account of their losses.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Every Union figure covers the whole raid, not Yellow Tavern alone.

open_questions: Stuart's, Fitzhugh Lee's and the Union division reports, the revised casualty return for Sheridan's first expedition (p.184) and any Confederate return remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan, and it shares headquarters papers with Meade's and Sheridan's reports. Meade's, Sheridan's, Hampton's, Butler's and Wild's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Parts 1 and 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
